saints.name: Olga of Kwethluk
saints.sourceTitle: Righteous Mother Olga of Kwethluk–Tanqilria Arrsamquq–Wonderworker, Matushka of All Alaska

summary.text: Olga Michael of Kwethluk is remembered as a Yup'ik mother, priest's wife, and midwife whose service centered on her Alaskan community. The OCA life recounts her care for families and people experiencing suffering. The official feast-day announcement fixes her commemoration on October 27, distinct from the November 8 civil date of her repose. Her modern glorification and published life are identified separately from earlier saints' narratives.

blocks.text: Olga (Arrsamquq) was born in Kwethluk in 1916. She married Nicolai Michael, later an Orthodox priest. Her work included food preparation, sewing, and care for children.

blocks.text: She served as a midwife and helped people with material needs, especially women carrying grief or suffering from abuse. As a priest’s wife she was called Matushka. The church account also transmits later testimonies of healing encounters and dreams associated with her intercession.

blocks.text: She died at home in Kwethluk on November 8, 1979, surrounded by family. Her death is not described as martyrdom. Her appointed feast day differs from her civil date of repose.

blocks.text: The OCA’s report of the actual glorification describes clergy and pilgrims reaching Kwethluk by air to Bethel and then by boat. On June 19, 2025, a final memorial service at Olga’s grave preceded the procession of her relics to Saint Nicholas Church. The proclamation was read there, and the vigil followed; the Divine Liturgy was celebrated the next morning. Village residents hosted the visitors at their school. The celebrations then continued in Anchorage. This locates formal public recognition in the same village community in which she lived.
